recall_prompt: Say how you would find n when 10 times n C 2 equals 3 times n plus 1 C 3.
insider_note: ⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾C₃ expands to exactly three factors, (n + 1)n(n − 1)/6, and the question is built around writing four. Once n(n − 1) is cancelled the equation is a single line.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write both combinations as products
steps.margin_note: First mark. ⁿC₂ = n(n − 1)/2 and ⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾C₃ = (n + 1)n(n − 1)/6. Both sides contain n(n − 1).

recall.must_convey: That n C 2 is n times n minus 1 over 2 and n plus 1 C 3 is n plus 1 times n times n minus 1 over 6, so the equation becomes 5 n times n minus 1 equals half of n plus 1 times n times n minus 1.
accept: n C two is n into n minus one by two and n plus one C three is n plus one into n into n minus one by six, so five n n minus one equals n plus one n n minus one by two
write both combinations as products, both sides have n into n minus one
ten by two is five on the left and three by six is half on the right
rendu C lanu products ga rayali, n into n minus one common
expand n C two and n plus one C three

steps.why: Both combinations contain the product n(n − 1); writing them out makes that shared factor visible so it can be cancelled in the next step.
common_mistakes: Writing ⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾C₃ as (n + 1)n(n − 1)(n − 2)/6 — three factors, not four.
Dropping the 10 or the 3 when simplifying the coefficients.

steps.label: Cancel n(n − 1) and solve
steps.margin_note: Second mark. n(n − 1) is not zero (n ≥ 2), so divide it out: 10 = n + 1 and n = 9.

recall.must_convey: That n times n minus 1 is not zero and is cancelled, leaving 10 = n plus 1, so n = 9.
accept: cancel n into n minus one from both sides to get ten equals n plus one so n is nine
divide out the common factor, ten is n plus one
n n minus one cancel cheste ten equal n plus one, n nine

steps.why: n(n − 1) can be divided out only because n ≥ 2 for ⁿC₂ to exist, so it is not zero. Saying so is what makes the cancellation legal.
common_mistakes: Answering n = 10 from "10 = n + 1" by not subtracting 1.
